- Exact-byte hash/size consistency, CRLF, BOM, Unicode, invalid UTF-8, NUL and content privacy.
- SQL scoping, lock order and fresh ownership recheck.
- Migration upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade and metadata drift.
- Actual composite constraints and one-active partial index.
- Concurrent creation of distinct and identical content.
- Revision plus job transaction rollback.
- Failed replacement preserves the active revision.
- Out-of-order and concurrent activations leave one consistent active pointer.
- Rollback after demotion but before promotion.
- Rollback when activation or final job success fails.
- Stale attempt refusal.
- Lease expiry during a document-lock wait.
- Lock-timeout mapping.
- Duplicate activation using a valid fenced invocation.
- Worker atomic-finish integration with test-only handlers.
- Both uncertain-commit cases using controlled doubles.

Use guarded disposable fixtures, event-controlled concurrency, bounded waits and test-only statement timeouts.

A. Endpoint scope and contracts

- POST /v1/vendors/{id}/documents
- GET /v1/documents/{id}
- GET /v1/documents/{id}/revisions/{rev}/chunks
- GET /v1/jobs/{id}

- payload revision_id;

Do not always label a duplicate response pending.

Define tenant-scoped queries and API database integration:

- stable ordering with tie-breakers;

- explicit handling of database failures;
- blocking database work kept off the event loop.

Document views exclude raw source content.

Chunk views may expose text for authorized inspection, with the accepted section, line, character and repeated-header provenance. Specify whether partial/failed ingestion chunks are visible and how their completeness is represented. Never imply a repeated-header chunk is one contiguous source passage.

Job views expose only reviewed operational fields. Do not expose raw payloads, owner identifiers, idempotency keys, exception text or unrestricted error details.

GET operations must not create jobs, change revision state or repair data.

E. Required ingestion_state projection

Implement the accepted M3d section E design in M3e:
- settled revision states take precedence;
- unsettled plus queued job → queued;
- unsettled plus running job → in_progress, including expired leases, without a progress guarantee;
- unsettled plus dead/failed/succeeded or missing canonical job → stalled.

3. Correct read consistency

A. Chunk pagination

Remove the blanket claim that chunk pages are stable because individual rows are immutable.

An unsettled revision can receive additional chunk batches. Its count and page contents can change between requests.

Specify:
- stable ordinal ordering;
- partial-set pages are observations at a particular read snapshot;
- no cross-request snapshot guarantee while writes continue;
- settled chunk sets are immutable under the application invariant;
- verified_complete is not inferred merely from a matching row count.

Preserve the accepted visibility policy and repeated-header provenance.

B. One consistent snapshot per GET response

“One transaction” at default READ COMMITTED is insufficient when several SELECTs build one response.

Specify a short REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction for the M3e read operations, established before their first data query. Keep the upload write transaction at the existing isolation.

Within one GET response, use the same snapshot for:
- parent existence checks;
- document pointers and active/latest revision views;
- canonical job and ingestion_state;
- chunk-set metadata, stored_count, total and items.

Capture one database-time value for lease-expired calculations within that response.

Do not keep transactions open while sending response bodies. Define how connection-level settings are scoped/reset so pooled connections do not leak isolation or read-only settings into later writes.

This guarantees internal consistency within one response, not a shared snapshot across separate HTTP requests.

C. Upload response observation time

Specify exactly when the UploadResult state is observed:
- construct one internally consistent response snapshot within the creation transaction after the required writes;
- send it only after successful commit;
- do not independently re-read selected fields after commit and mix observation times.

A worker may change the state immediately after commit. Explain that the response reports the observed snapshot, not a promise that the state will remain pending or queued.

Preserve 202 for newly created revisions and 200 for duplicates.

Add planned PostgreSQL concurrency tests for:
- activation between document-view reads;
- a chunk batch committing between count and page reads;
- consistent revision/job projection;
- pooled-connection settings restored before a later upload write.

4. Tighten the multipart contract

A. Explicit parser completion

Specify validation of:
- required disposition headers and field names;
- syntactically valid boundary parameters;
- final closing boundary;
- truncated headers or part data;
- client disconnect.

Do not assume that calling MultipartParser.finalize() necessarily detects every truncated body. Implementation must verify the selected library’s actual behavior and explicitly track parser completion where needed.

No success response is allowed for a truncated multipart body.

B. Content-Length

Keep streaming byte counts authoritative for size enforcement.

When Content-Length is present and the ASGI server provides a normal completed stream, require the actual received body length to match it; otherwise 400.

For disconnects or transport rejection, abort without database writes. Do not guarantee a response can always be delivered after disconnect.

Tests may use controlled ASGI streams for mismatches a production HTTP server would reject before the application sees them.

C. Error precedence and bounds

Make the current precedence implementable:
- duplicate/unknown fields and a second file are structural 422 errors;
- exceeding a part-count or byte cap is 413;
- malformed parser input may prevent further meaningful parsing.

Specify which errors are deferred while bounded parsing continues and which terminate immediately. Do not promise that a later cap violation overrides an earlier parser failure after reading has already stopped.

Retain bounded memory and immediate enforcement of hard caps. Never drain an arbitrarily large invalid request solely to establish global error precedence.

Add mixed-fault tests with exact expected outcomes, including:
- duplicate field followed by excess parts;
- malformed multipart before a later oversized tail;
- missing closing boundary despite otherwise valid fields;
- short/long declared lengths with a normally completed ASGI stream.

5. Clarify dependency and privacy wording

The reviewer accepts using an established streaming multipart library in principle. No dependency is installed or selected by this prompt.

Keep release-age, compatibility and advisory checks as implementation prerequisites. Do not bypass the age policy or add a newer release silently.

Correct the broad privacy-test statement:
- errors and logs must not contain submitted content, filenames, arbitrary field names, values or internal exceptions;
- authorized successful responses intentionally contain documented metadata and, for ChunkView, chunk text;
- document views exclude raw source content;
- job views exclude the specified internal fields.

Add tests for both safe error/log behavior and intended authorized success fields.

7. File-based handoff

Export the complete incremental diff against:
89a9b73396f2b597e78ae143a69e52643170f75e

Exclude prompts.md and save as:
.local/p87/m3e-spec-corrections.diff

Use UTF-8 without BOM. Do not print the diff.

Report the changes, actual checks, branch, HEAD, new staged tree, staged paths, file size and SHA-256.

End with:

- **Header-byte cap:** the per-part 8 KiB cap now counts the raw header region. That is every byte the parser consumes in a header state, from after the boundary line's line ending through the empty line's line ending, inclusive. It no longer counts callback-reported names and values plus a synthetic overhead. The feeder already sends header regions one byte at a time, so it refuses the byte that crosses the cap before the parser sees it. Earlier malformed bytes still win, and the result does not depend on receive partitioning.
- **Parameters:** a strict RFC 9110 parameter parser keeps extended and repeated parameters, and replaces `parse_options_header` for the request `Content-Type`, the part `Content-Disposition` and the file `Content-Type`. As a result:
  - `filename*` on a text field is a 422;
  - `charset*` and repeated or conflicting `charset` parameters are deferred 415s;
  - repeated, extended or missing disposition `name` parameters are 422;
  - repeated or extended `boundary` parameters are 415.

  - a later upload writing on the same pooled connection after a snapshot;
  - duplicates of processing, superseded, failed and dead-job revisions;
  - GET never repairing a missing job, while a duplicate POST does;
  - the upload observation boundary;
  - terminal jobs with unsettled revisions;

- Validate M4a provider values first.

- Vector writes/readiness require the real job fence, kind index_revision and exactly the validated index_id payload.

- Respect job → index lock order.
- Recheck fresh ownership after waits on every successful path, including no-ops.
- Reject writes to ready indexes.
- Compare replayed immutable fields; never overwrite conflicting rows.
- Completeness checks exact source membership/manifests, profile identity and stored-vector manifest, not count alone.
- Reuse the accepted public chunk query/manifest helpers without changing M3 activation locking.
- Readiness and job success must be capable of committing atomically through the existing fence.

The detailed proposal must resolve or explicitly present for review:

### Enqueue and bounded backfill
- Exact internal function signatures, trusted actor/tenant inputs and authorization responsibilities.
- Deterministic idempotency key and behavior for existing building/ready indexes and queued/running/terminal jobs.
- No resetting terminal jobs or silently replacing conflicting identities.
- What happens when a building index has a missing, failed or dead canonical job.
- Explicit bounded selection, ordering, pagination/cursor and transaction boundaries.
- Whether M4c exposes a CLI or an internal seam only, with a recommendation.
- Whether activation wiring is deferred or proposed now; do not silently change M3 activation.
- Concurrency and atomicity of duplicate enqueue/backfill requests.

### Handler and provider selection
- Exact production registry integration and supported initial profile.
- Resolve the provider from the stored identity through a fixed supported mapping.
- Reject unsupported/mismatched profiles without importing a live adapter or making network calls.
- Use M4a's validated provider boundary and M4b's canonical storage conversion.
- Specify injected provider doubles for tests while preserving production defaults.
- No provider identifiers, document text or credentials in job payloads.

### Batching, replay and completeness
- Bounded source reads and provider batches respecting both the 32-text and 128,000-byte caps.
- Stable ordinal ordering and text-hash verification.
- Read/connection lifetimes: no database transaction or job/index lock held during provider computation.
- Read and reuse already committed embeddings; do not recompute or overwrite them on retry.
- Missing-row processing and conflicting replay behavior.
- Short fenced writes with the accepted job → index lock order.
- Exact final completeness and atomic readiness/job success.
- Already-ready retry behavior and fresh ownership checks.
- Explain the limit: repeated uncommitted computation can occur; no exactly-once provider-call claim.

### Cancellation and failures
- Cancellation checks before and after provider work, before writes and before final completion.
- Lease loss and cancellation cause no stale writes or terminal outcome.
- Map invalid provider output, unsupported profile, source inconsistency, storage conflict and transient/unexpected failure to explicit existing or proposed fixed error codes.
- Distinguish retryable from permanent outcomes and exhausted/dead behavior.
- Preserve existing worker shutdown semantics; synchronous calls do not gain a guaranteed total deadline.
- Privacy: no raw text, vectors, keys or exception details in logs, outcomes or representations.

### Proposed implementation and tests
- Intended modules and minimal changes to existing files.
- Whether any migration or configuration change is needed, with justification.
- ADR-0015 as a later implementation deliverable, not a new file in this task.
- Database-independent tests for provider selection, caps, replay, cancellation, safe failures and handler registration.
- Deterministic PostgreSQL tests for enqueue atomicity/concurrency, partial committed batches, retry reuse, conflicts, stale leases, readiness/job atomicity and terminal-job behavior.
- Production-path offline indexing verification, distinct from the existing ingestion smoke.
- Installed-wheel checks appropriate to the new handler.
- Mark every new test as planned, not executed.

## 4. Correct source facts and enqueue outcomes

### Ready-index behavior

The facts section incorrectly says write_embeddings and mark_index_ready both treat a ready index as a no-op.

Correct it:
- write_embeddings refuses writes to a ready index with EmbeddingWriteRefusedError;
- mark_index_ready provides the fresh-ownership-checked already-ready no-op.

### Enqueue results

The existing enqueue function returns only JobSnapshot. It does not say whether this invocation inserted the job. A pre-read cannot establish that reliably under concurrent enqueue, and queued/attempt-zero state does not distinguish creation from an existing untouched job.

Simplify the proposed IndexEnqueueResult outcome to:
- `pending`: canonical job is queued or running, whether newly created or already present;
- `ready`: index observed ready; no new job is enqueued;
- `stalled`: building index with an existing terminal canonical job.

Keep the job snapshot where appropriate. Do not add a creation flag to M3a enqueue or infer creation from timestamps, attempts, pre-reads or PostgreSQL system columns.

Retain:
- atomic index creation and enqueue;
- deterministic idempotency key;
- missing-job creation for a building index;
- terminal-job immutability;
- idempotency conflicts with transaction rollback.

Describe the returned status as an observation within the transaction, not a promise that the job stays queued/running after commit.

Correct the isolation wording: the supported seam uses READ COMMITTED. Stronger isolation can also produce database serialization failures; do not imply every concurrency failure becomes JobEnqueueRaceError.

Update CLI counts, result types and planned tests to match the simplified outcomes.

## 5. Make backfill and CLI behavior precise

Specify:
- validate actor, identity, limit and cursor before starting writes;
- all selection and enqueue queries remain tenant-scoped;
- each selected revision has an independent write transaction;
- fixed per-item `ineligible` and `conflict` outcomes apply only to explicitly named expected domain failures;
- rollback that item's transaction before continuing;
- unexpected database, programming or infrastructure failures propagate and fail the operation, rather than becoming a successful per-item result.

A per-item failure may have no index ID because its transaction rolled back. Make index_id nullable for those results.

Clarify partial progress: previously committed items remain committed if a later unexpected failure aborts the operation. No all-page atomicity claim.

Clarify selection races:
- revisions are active at the selection observation;
- if a selected revision becomes superseded before its enqueue transaction, it may still be indexed because it was activated and its chunks are immutable;
- do not claim it remains active throughout the run;
- revisions already superseded at selection are excluded from ordinary backfill;
- explicit enqueue continues to allow ever-activated superseded revisions.

The cursor advances over selected IDs, including per-item failures. A retry of skipped/conflicted candidates may require restarting from the beginning. Newly activated UUIDs below the cursor can also require a fresh pass.

Define CLI behavior:
- one bounded page per invocation;
- prints fixed outcome counts and next cursor only;
- existing argparse validation and privacy conventions;
- exit 0 for a page without stalled/ineligible/conflict results;
- nonzero for stalled/ineligible/conflict or an unexpected operation failure;
- no raw exception text or content;
- no automatic retry loop or terminal-job recovery.

## 6. Correct cancellation and transaction guarantees

The current JobContext checks local cancellation/lease state at explicit boundaries. It does not atomically guard every SQL statement or interrupt statements already in flight.

Remove the claim that a latched cancellation prevents “any further write or terminal outcome” without qualification.

State the actual guarantees:
- explicit checks before and after provider computation;
- fenced entry checks before opening and after acquiring the job lock;
- another local check before success in a finish=True block;
- database ownership checks remain authoritative;
- cancellation latched after the last applicable check may not stop an already-started non-finish transaction from committing;
- checks do not interrupt synchronous provider or database calls;
- the existing accepted lease-expiry/commit window and shutdown limitations remain.

A cancellation may cause the runtime to record retryable worker_shutdown while ownership remains valid. Do not claim cancellation produces no lifecycle outcome. Lease loss prevents an outcome by the stale worker.

Specify the provider-exception path:
- when provider execution or validation raises, check ctx.check() before converting that failure into PermanentJobError or RetryableJobError;
- a cancellation or lease loss already latched during that call must take precedence over classification of the provider failure;
- preserve control-flow exceptions;
- acknowledge the same explicit-boundary race rather than claiming atomic cancellation.

The calls using ctx.fenced() for reads still acquire the job-row lock and use the ordinary fenced transaction. Call them “short read-purpose fenced transactions”, not PostgreSQL READ ONLY transactions. Add no SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY.

Hash verification, batch canonicalization and provider computation should occur after the read fence closes, keeping the job lock short.

Planned tests must cover:
- cancellation or lease loss before provider work;
- successful provider return after cancellation/lease loss;
- provider/validation failure after cancellation/lease loss is latched;
- before-write and before-finish boundaries;
- actual runtime outcome semantics;
- the documented limitations without inventing stronger guarantees.

## 7. Correct replay and provider-selection details

The proposed handler skips already-committed embeddings. Therefore it cannot generally discover that an existing valid stored vector differs from a newly computed provider vector without recomputing it.

Preserve reuse:
- previously committed valid rows are reused without provider calls;
- do not promise semantic or provider-output verification of reused vectors;
- M4b constraints bind stored bytes, profile and source membership, not the semantic correctness of an embedding.

Replace the ambiguous planned test “a conflicting pre-existing row gives a permanent failure” with two precise tests:
1. A previously committed row is reused without recomputation, and remains unchanged.
2. A controlled competing writer commits a different valid vector after a missing chunk has been selected but before this attempt's write. The M4b replay comparison detects the conflict, nothing is overwritten, and the handler records the specified permanent failure while ownership remains valid.

Use a separate valid job/fence for the competing writer and deterministic barriers/hooks, not a reclaimed stale owner that is expected to write successfully.

Make the provider mapping immutable or defensively copied when the handler factory is created, including injected test mappings.

Require stored identity reconstruction and fingerprint verification before provider resolution. Provider identity must match the captured stored identity. No live adapter or environment-based selection.

Use privacy-safe source-page values whose representations omit text, and preserve tenant/revision/chunker scoping for every read.

## 3. Persistence and operator seam

Implement evidenceguard_persistence/indexing.py with the accepted boundaries.

### Enqueue
- Tenant comes only from the validated actor.
- Existing reviewer, approver or admin roles.
- Caller-owned READ COMMITTED transaction; no commit inside the seam.
- ensure_profile/create_index plus canonical enqueue atomically.
- Payload exactly index_id, idempotency key str(index.id).
- Outcomes pending, ready or stalled as transaction observations.
- No inferred “created” flag and no M3a enqueue redesign.
- Missing canonical job for a building index is created.
- Existing terminal jobs remain unchanged.
- Ready indexes enqueue nothing.
- Conflicts propagate and roll back the caller's transaction.

### Backfill
- Validate actor, identity, limit and cursor before transactions.
- One bounded tenant-scoped selection page.
- Active at selection, with a chunk set and no ready index for the profile.
- UUID ordering/cursor and accepted limit 50, maximum 100.
- One independent write transaction per selected revision.
- Only the named expected failures become ineligible/conflict after rollback.
- Unexpected failures propagate; earlier committed items remain committed.
- Nullable index_id for failed items.
- Preserve the accepted supersession-race and cursor limitations.

### CLI
Add eg-admin backfill-indexes using the existing trusted-operator model and fixed HASH_IDENTITY.

One page per invocation. Print fixed outcome counts and next cursor only.

Exit codes:
- 0: clean completed page;
- 3: completed page containing stalled/ineligible/conflict;
- 1: operation failure;
- 2: usage error.

Retain existing argparse safety, import boundaries and privacy conventions. No automatic retry or terminal-job reset.

- Tests inject doubles through the handler factory and test-owned registries.

Use short read-purpose ctx.fenced() transactions. They hold the job-row lock and are not PostgreSQL READ ONLY transactions.

After the read fence closes:
- retain the longest prefix within both 32 chunks and 128,000 UTF-8 bytes;
- verify source text hashes;
- check cancellation/lease state;

- write through M4b in a short fenced transaction.

## 2. Preserve provider control-flow exceptions

In apps/worker/evidenceguard_worker/indexing.py, resolve_provider currently catches every Exception from the factory and provider.identity validation and converts it to UnsupportedProfileError.

This includes JobCancelledError, LeaseLostError and FenceClosedError, contradicting the accepted requirement that these control-flow exceptions propagate untouched.

Correct the factory/identity-resolution boundary:
- explicitly preserve those three exception types;
- preserve BaseException control flow;
- retain fixed, private handling of ordinary factory or identity failures;
- do not expose the original factory exception or its text through the outward error chain.

Also cover cancellation or lease loss latched during a factory/identity operation that raises an ordinary exception:
- check ctx.check() before classifying the resulting expected profile failure as PermanentJobError;
- a previously latched cancellation or lease loss must win;
- retain the accepted explicit-boundary race limitations.

Choose a small implementation consistent with the existing handler structure. Do not redesign M4a's provider boundary or worker runtime.

Do not turn all unexpected errors into permanent failures.

## 3. Add meaningful regression tests

Extend tests/test_index_handler.py to cover:

1. A provider factory raises each of:
   - JobCancelledError;
   - LeaseLostError;
   - FenceClosedError.

   The same control-flow exception must escape, rather than UnsupportedProfileError or PermanentJobError.

2. A provider's identity property raises the same three control-flow exceptions, with the same propagation requirement.

3. A factory or identity operation latches cancellation or lease loss, then raises an ordinary exception:
   - ctx.check() takes precedence before permanent classification;
   - no page read, embedding write or success follows.

4. An ordinary factory/identity failure without a latch remains a fixed permanent failure:
   - no submitted marker or original exception text leaks through the surfaced error/traceback chain.

Retain existing successful provider selection, identity mismatch and immutable-mapping tests.

Run the new regression cases against the Prompt 125 handler temporarily and record which fail. Restore the corrected handler and verify its saved hash before continuing.

Use ignored local copies for this comparison. Do not reset the index or overwrite unrelated staged work.

## 4. Make PostgreSQL cancellation verification deterministic

In tests/test_indexing_postgres.py,
test_cancellation_while_the_provider_blocks_records_worker_shutdown_and_writes_nothing
currently uses:

time.sleep(1.0)

to assume the runtime requested cancellation after its drain period.

Replace that assumption with an observed synchronization condition:
- keep the provider blocked;
- request shutdown;
- wait with a bounded deadline until the actual attempt's cancellation state is latched;
- assert that state was observed;
- only then release the provider.

Use a test-owned handler wrapper, captured JobContext, event or equivalent narrow test instrumentation. Do not change production worker semantics or add a test-only production API.

Ensure the provider is released in finally, including when an assertion or wait fails, and bound all waits.

Continue to assert the actual database outcome:

- index remains building;
- job is queued with worker_shutdown while ownership remains valid.

### Inspect the actual boundaries

Read the relevant:
- actor, tenant and role contracts;
- embedding identity, validation, provider and canonical-storage modules;

### Accepted policy to preserve

1. Snapshot capture is trusted and tenant/vendor scoped.
2. Capture selects the vendor’s active revision pointers, complete immutable chunk sets and ready indexes for the pinned profile in one consistent read transaction.
3. If any active revision lacks the required complete/ready state, refuse capture rather than silently omit it.
4. Record the accepted pending/processing exclusions with precise semantics.
5. An empty eligible set is an explicit error.
6. A manually supplied revision-ID list alone proves neither authorization nor past eligibility.
7. A revision active at capture remains eligible for that snapshot after later supersession.
8. A revision already superseded at capture is excluded from a new snapshot.
9. New revisions never enter an older snapshot.
10. Current-state search first captures a fresh snapshot.
11. Never-activated, failed, incomplete, foreign-tenant/vendor, wrong-profile and non-snapshot chunks remain excluded.

M5 persists snapshot/review authorization and configuration facts. Do not implement or design a new review API in M4d.

### Snapshot contract and trust boundary

Specify:
- trusted actor-derived tenant and vendor checks;
- explicit revision/index/chunk-set bindings;
- profile identity/fingerprint;
- chunk counts and manifests;
- retrieval configuration/version;
- provenance needed to validate and reuse the snapshot;
- duplicate and malformed-ID handling;
- immutable values and safe representations.

Explain where authoritative eligibility is established and what constructors can validate structurally.

Do not equate a frozen object, UUID list or hash with an authorization capability. Explain how later retrieval verifies tenant/vendor ownership and immutable bindings while preserving snapshot-relative supersession.

State the trust model and any persistence/provenance limitation that remains until M5. If a policy cannot be enforced without additional machinery, present the issue and recommendation for review.

Specify race behaviour for activation during capture and supersession after capture.

### Transactions and provider work

Propose an implementable consistency model:
- short consistent read transactions for capture and retrieval;
- exact transaction settings and their first-statement requirements;
- one response/result’s counts, eligibility checks and channel queries must not contradict one another;
- transaction-scoped settings restored on pooled connections;
- provider calls and expensive Python work outside database transactions;
- no writes or implicit indexing from capture/retrieval.

Explain the sequence for validating input, obtaining query embeddings, opening read transactions and validating snapshot bindings. Handle changes between those stages explicitly.

Do not claim consistency across separate requests or an atomic boundary spanning a provider call and a database transaction.

### Accepted input and corpus bounds

Preserve:
- 1–8 distinct nonblank queries;
- each at most 4,000 code points and 16,000 UTF-8 bytes;
- 1–100 distinct revision IDs;
- at most 100,000 eligible chunks;
- reject excess instead of silently truncating;
- per-channel candidate limit 20;
- requested final k 1–20, default 8.

Specify strict types, unknown fields, booleans/coercions, UTF-8/NUL handling, query distinctness, total batching and fixed validation errors.

Explain how capture detects bound violations without accidentally accepting a truncated set.

These are engineering defaults, not performance measurements.

### Lexical and vector channels

Specify concrete SQL/data flow and score meaning:
- explicit PostgreSQL simple configuration for documents and queries;
- a recommended query constructor and its exact query semantics;
- exact pgvector cosine operations, no approximate index;

The choices are settled; the corrected specification as a whole remains pending review.

## Correction 1: Make transaction order match the existing helper

The existing document_views.read_snapshot helper executes:
1. SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY
2. SELECT clock_timestamp()
3. yields the session and captured time

The proposal currently says this unchanged helper will set statement_timeout before clock_timestamp. It cannot do that.

Specify the implementable order when reusing the helper unchanged:
1. isolation/read-only statement;
2. its single clock_timestamp query;
3. SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 30000 after the helper yields;
4. capture or retrieval data statements.

The repeatable-read snapshot is established by the first snapshot-taking SELECT, including the helper’s clock_timestamp SELECT. Do not say it starts only at the later vendor query.

captured_at is informational, not an exact proof of the snapshot’s visibility or past eligibility.

Update race descriptions and planned interleaving tests accordingly. Hooks must be positioned relative to the actual snapshot establishment.

Remove the blanket claim that capture never blocks or is blocked. Ordinary SELECTs take relation locks and can conflict with DDL. State the narrower guarantee: no explicit row locks and no row-lock conflict with ordinary activation/indexing DML.

The 30-second timeout is per statement, not a whole-retrieval or provider-call deadline. State that explicitly. Do not promise an overall execution bound or add an unreviewed retry loop.

Keep transaction-local settings and pooled restoration requirements.

## Correction 2: Correct canonical conversion and standalone validation

The actual signature is:
canonical_vector(vector, *, allows_zero: bool)

Replace the proposed allows_zero keyword with allows_zero throughout the specification.

Separate the contracts of:
- search_snapshot, which receives an actual provider;
- retrieve_with_vectors, which receives a precomputed EmbeddingBatch and has no provider object.

The standalone persistence seam must independently validate:
- actor, role and tenant scope;
- request and snapshot structure;
- batch identity against the snapshot;
- input_type == "query";
- vector count against request query count;
- numeric/dimension rules;
- canonical float32 conversion.

It must not refer to a provider.identity property it cannot access.

Retain conversion outside the database transaction. Reuse the existing numeric tolerance and zero policy; no renormalization or tolerance widening.

Clarify that validation cannot prove that caller-supplied vectors were computed from the claimed query strings. The precomputed-vector seam is trusted internal input.

## Correction 3: Specify the provider-property exception boundary

The initial provider.identity access can itself raise, before embed_validated is called.

Specify privacy-safe handling for ordinary exceptions during:
- provider identity access and validation;
- the embedding call;
- result validation;
- canonical conversion.

They must become fixed RetrievalProviderError messages without the original exception retained as cause or context, following the existing outside-except pattern.

Do not claim the initial property access is already protected by embed_validated.

Define the scope precisely:
- no new JobContext or worker cancellation protocol in M4d;
- no broad BaseException catch;
- no changes to M4a or M4c control-flow semantics;
- existing embed_validated behaviour is described accurately.

Add planned cases for an identity getter throwing an exception containing a private marker, identity mismatch before any call, an identity changing between reads, malformed results and numeric conversion failure.

## Correction 4: Remove unsafe raw database-exception propagation

Delete the claim that SQLAlchemyError may propagate unchanged safely because hide_parameters=True.

That option hides parameter formatting in SQLAlchemy logging/StatementError strings. It does not sanitize arbitrary database/driver messages, exception attributes or exception chains.

Specify a fixed, content-free database failure boundary for the new retrieval seams, for example RetrievalDatabaseError with a fixed code.

Cover:
- session acquisition and statement execution;
- timeout and connection failures;
- row conversion where backend-originated values may appear in exceptions;
- transaction cleanup.

Do not expose original driver messages, statements, parameters, vectors, query text or exception chains.

Keep the original failure primary if cleanup also fails, with no raw cleanup exception escaping or being logged.

Do not add automatic retries. A database failure must not become a successful empty result.

Map known semantic validation failures to their existing fixed retrieval errors; distinguish those from operational database failures.

Add planned fake-session privacy tests with markers in exception text, statement/parameters and chained exceptions, plus timeout and cleanup-failure cases.

Keep the engine’s existing hide_parameters setting as defence in depth. No engine or workflow change in this task.

Useful official reference:
https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/engines.html#sqlalchemy.create_engine.params.hide_parameters

## Correction 5: Complete canonical hashing and value contracts

The proposal names config_sha256 and snapshot_sha256 but does not define their canonical byte representation.

Specify a versioned canonical encoding:
- exact field names and nesting;
- UUID and digest representation;
- UTC datetime encoding and precision;
- ordered bindings and exclusion IDs;
- integer and boolean handling;
- identity/config representation;
- UTF-8 JSON rules, sorted keys and compact separators;
- digest fields excluded from their own input;
- no Python repr, hash(), locale or default=str.

Prefer deriving digests internally from validated fields rather than trusting a caller-supplied digest. If externally supplied digests remain supported, define their exact verification.

Make the exclusion record a named immutable value with explicit fields, bounds and count/truncated invariants.

Complete the important structural invariants for:
- RevisionBinding and snapshot bindings, including one binding per document;
- ChannelHit and channel lists;
- finite scores and channel-specific ordering;
- query-position and rank bounds;
- duplicate list/entry rejection;
- final result IDs, ranks, counts and provenance consistency.

Do not require a vector distance range narrower than the actual operator’s numeric behaviour without evidence; reject non-finite scores and document numeric assumptions.

Retain exact Fraction comparisons for fusion and float display only.

Add independently pinned canonical bytes/digests and invalid-value fixtures to the planned tests. No probes or tests need to run now.

## Correction 6: Make SQL guarantees and test coverage explicit

The SQL examples currently rely on prior binding verification to establish vendor ownership.

State that dependency clearly, and show or describe the complete joins/filters connecting:
- tenant;
- vendor-owned document;
- revision;
- snapshot binding;
- ready index;
- pinned profile;
- matching embedding/chunk row.

Apply eligibility before each channel’s ORDER BY/LIMIT.

Preserve old-snapshot supersession behaviour: do not add a current-active filter.

Add real PostgreSQL planned tests for:
- lexical query semantics: AND, quoted phrase, OR, negation-only and punctuation-only input;
- positive-score filtering;
- simple-configuration behaviour;
- exact cosine ordering using independently chosen vectors;
- equal-distance and equal-lexical-score UUID tie ordering;
- stored-zero exclusion and zero-query lexical fallback;
- multiple-query/channel fusion against independently calculated expected ranks;
- eligible candidates surviving more than 20 higher-scoring forbidden candidates;
- ready indexes for multiple profiles without duplicate lexical candidates.

Pure fusion fixtures do not establish that the PostgreSQL statements rank and filter correctly.

Make capture error precedence independent of row iteration order: validate each phase across the selected set before moving to the next phase.

Document source-corruption assumptions rather than claiming hashes or immutable application conventions protect against arbitrary direct database modification.

## Final clarification 1: Preserve the primary failure explicitly

Replace the database-boundary prescription that discovers a semantic outcome by searching an arbitrary exception chain.

Specify an explicit pending outcome:
- record the semantic error code or operational failure classification from the transaction body before leaving it;
- attempt transaction cleanup;
- if the body failed, its recorded classification stays primary even if cleanup also fails;
- if the body succeeded but cleanup fails, return no result and raise fixed RetrievalDatabaseError;
- raise a fresh fixed error outside exception handlers, retaining no original exception objects or chains.

Do not infer the primary semantic outcome merely because a semantic-looking exception occurs somewhere in a backend exception’s context or cause chain.

Keep the existing read_snapshot helper unchanged. The new seam’s wrapper may manage its pending outcome around that helper.

Ordinary database failures are normalized. Process-control BaseException subclasses must not be converted into RetrievalDatabaseError or successful results.

Retain the planned tests for semantic failure plus cleanup failure, operational failure plus cleanup failure, and successful work plus cleanup failure. Add a case where a backend exception happens to have a semantic error in its chain: it must remain an operational failure unless the seam itself recorded that semantic outcome.

This specifies failure precedence, not a new retry or cancellation protocol. M5 job cancellation/lease integration remains deferred.

## Final clarification 2: Do not promise digest uniqueness

Replace:
“two captures of identical facts have different digests”

with the precise rule:
- captured_at is included in the canonical snapshot encoding;
- captures with different encoded timestamps can have different canonical bytes even when their other facts match;
- captures with identical encoded fields produce the same digest;
- timestamps have finite precision and are not unique IDs;
- neither timestamp nor digest proves authorization, past eligibility or uniqueness.

Do not add random IDs, HMACs, secrets or persistence.

## Implementation requirements

### Domain contracts and hashing

Implement the accepted frozen values, strict validation, query conversion and pure fusion.

Preserve:
- exact types without coercion;
- immutable tuples and revalidation;
- verbatim input strings;
- fixed private errors;
- content-free representations;
- derived profile/config/snapshot identifiers and digests;
- the exact eg-retrieval-canonical-v1 encoding;
- UTC timestamp precision and field sets;
- exclusion count/IDs/truncated invariants;
- one binding per document;
- channel/result ordering and consistency rules.

Digests are computed internally. A digest or timestamp is not authorization, proof of past eligibility or a unique capture identifier.

Use independently pinned canonical fixtures. Do not generate expected values by calling the implementation under test.

### Capture

Implement capture_snapshot with:
- trusted actor-derived tenant;
- reviewer/approver roles only;
- vendor-scoped active pointers;
- verified chunk-set bindings and ready indexes for the pinned identity;
- refusal if any active revision is unready;
- explicit empty-set error;
- 101-row excess detection for the 100-revision bound;
- rejection above 100,000 eligible chunks;
- bounded exclusion IDs with an exact count;
- phase-wide deterministic error precedence.

Use the unchanged read_snapshot helper:
1. transaction isolation/read-only statement;
2. its clock_timestamp SELECT establishes the snapshot;
3. transaction-local statement timeout;
4. capture data queries.

No writes, enqueue, indexing or explicit row locks.

### Retrieval and trust boundary

Implement retrieve_with_vectors, search_snapshot and search_current as specified.

Keep provider calls and canonical query conversion outside database transactions.

The standalone persistence seam validates its precomputed batch independently. It has no provider object and does not prove that supplied vectors were computed from the claimed query strings.

Before channel queries, recheck every immutable snapshot binding against the database.

Do not re-filter old snapshots by current active status:
- active at capture remains eligible after supersession;
- a new revision never enters an older snapshot.

Preserve the accepted interim trust limitation:
- internal trusted snapshots only;
- no endpoint or untrusted deserialization;
- binding checks cannot prove past active-at-capture eligibility;
- M5 persists and reloads capture facts through trusted paths;
- no malicious in-process-code protection claim.

### Channels, fusion and evidence

Implement:
- explicit simple full-text configuration;
- websearch_to_tsquery and positive ts_rank_cd scores;
- exact cosine distance with canonical float32 query bindings;
- exclusion of stored zero vectors;
- vector-skipped queries retaining their lexical channel;
- complete eligibility joins before each channel limit;
- at most 20 candidates per query/channel;
- exact Fraction RRF comparisons with constant 60;
- canonical UUID tie ordering;
- unique final chunks, bounded by requested k;
- channel/query ranks and scores;
- exact evidence text, verified digest, spans and provenance;
- separate repeated-header and body spans.

No approximate index, automatic fallback to a different profile, silent truncation or successful empty result on operational failure.

### Failure boundaries

Implement the accepted fixed provider and database errors.

Protect the first provider.identity access as well as embedding, result validation and canonical conversion.

Raise fresh fixed errors outside exception handlers; do not retain original causes, contexts or raw backend objects.

For database work:
- record the body’s semantic outcome or operational classification explicitly;
- retain the body failure as primary if cleanup also fails;
- successful work plus cleanup failure yields RetrievalDatabaseError;
- never classify an outcome by searching an arbitrary exception chain;
- no automatic retries;
- process-control BaseException subclasses are not normalized.

Keep read_snapshot unchanged.

Exercise setup, body and cleanup failures in fake-session tests. Verify primary-failure behaviour and process-control propagation, including interaction with cleanup, rather than relying only on the happy path.

No new JobContext integration or changes to M4a/M4c cancellation semantics. M5 integration remains deferred.

snapshot reference; the extra snapshot invariants; `search_current` obtaining the profile
identity before capture. The metadata-only `_chunk_heavy_vendor` fixture exception is approved
solely for testing capture's metadata-based chunk-count arithmetic; it may bypass ingestion
completeness and indexing readiness verification for that isolated bound test and proves neither
ingestion/indexing correctness nor stored-vector completeness. Prompt 134's records called it

## Fix 1: Preserve setup-time process control when cleanup fails

run_read currently records pending.control only inside the yielded transaction body.

If read_snapshot raises KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit or another non-Exception BaseException during either setup statement, then its rollback or close raises an ordinary exception, the outer handler sees only that cleanup failure and normalizes it.

Fix the boundary so process control raised during helper setup is not converted into RetrievalDatabaseError when ordinary cleanup fails.

Preserve:
- the unchanged read_snapshot helper;
- explicit pending semantic/operational outcomes;
- semantic outcomes determined by the seam’s own checks, never arbitrary exception-chain classification;
- ordinary setup/body/cleanup failures mapped to fresh fixed errors;
- no original database exception retained or logged;
- no retries;
- process-control exceptions propagated unconverted.

Any handling used to recover process control must remain distinct from classifying semantic errors. Do not restore the rejected practice of treating a semantic-looking exception in a backend chain as a semantic outcome.

Keep the change proportionate. Do not redesign transaction ownership or add a new cancellation protocol.

Add regression cases for:
- process control during SET TRANSACTION;
- process control during clock_timestamp;
- ordinary rollback failure while each propagates;
- ordinary close failure while each propagates;
- the same exception object escaping;
- cleanup being attempted;
- existing body-time and cleanup-time process-control behaviour remaining correct;
- ordinary setup exceptions still yielding private RetrievalDatabaseError.

Cover KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, or an equivalent explicit matrix that exercises both real classes.

## Fix 2: Make the chunk-bound fixture append distinct revisions

The existing test calls:

_chunk_heavy_vendor(..., 24)
_chunk_heavy_vendor(..., 1)

Both calls start at n=0 and reuse heavy-0 with identical content. create_revision therefore resolves the existing revision, and the following ChunkSet insert duplicates its primary key.

Give the fixture an explicit start/offset or another deterministic way to create distinct documents and content across calls.

Keep the test’s meaning:
- first 24 distinct revisions declare 98,304 chunks and capture succeeds;
- one additional distinct revision brings the total to 102,400 and capture raises SnapshotBoundsError.

Add assertions that the second phase actually contains 25 distinct documents/revisions/chunk sets/indexes for the fixture vendor, with the intended aggregate metadata count, before asserting the capture rejection.

Keep this exception local to the metadata-bound test. Other retrieval tests should continue using real ingestion and indexing paths.

The PostgreSQL test remains written and unexecuted until CI. Do not report an observed PostgreSQL failure or pass.

## Complete the planned PostgreSQL coverage

### Retrieval interleaving

Add a deterministic test that:
1. captures an eligible old revision;
2. starts retrieval on a dedicated engine;
3. pauses after the binding recheck, before the channel queries;
4. commits activation of a replacement through the real lifecycle on another connection;
5. resumes retrieval;
6. verifies channels and evidence still return the old snapshot revision and never the replacement.

Use bounded events/hooks, assert the hook fired, and release/remove everything in finally.

This complements the existing capture interleavings and supersession-before-retrieval tests. It must not depend on sleeps.

### Wrong-profile and building-index candidates before limits

The existing filters-before-limits test covers many high-scoring foreign-tenant, foreign-vendor and superseded candidates.

The separate profile/building test contains only a small number of rows. Add the accepted adversarial coverage with more than 20 tempting candidates from:
- a wrong-profile ready index;
- a building index with committed partial embeddings.

Use controlled vectors/text so the test establishes that those rows would outrank or displace a target if the relevant filter were omitted.

Verify the eligible target survives in both applicable channel lists and forbidden rows neither leak nor duplicate candidates.

Use the existing real enqueue/fenced-write patterns. Do not mark these indexes ready directly merely to simplify the test. If a building index is produced by an injected finish failure, assert the intended state and stored rows were actually produced.

Keep all new PostgreSQL cases integration-marked, with the existing disposable-database guards.

### A. Corpus and ground truth

Preserve section 7's fictional tenants and vendors, document roles and authenticity labels, conflicting retention evidence, superseded revision trap, missing answers, table content, wrong claims paired with valid but non-supporting quotations, foreign-tenant canaries and injected variant.

Specify:

- No real client documents, credentials or personal data.
- What labels are authored ground truth, rather than model judgments.
- No assumption that Markdown anchors can be inserted without affecting production chunking.

### B. Loading and lifecycle

Propose an explicit, bounded loading approach grounded in existing seams:
- Tenant-scoped records and role handling.
- Real revision creation, ingestion, activation and indexing.
- Correct supersession order and ready-index checks.
- Idempotency and repeat-invocation behaviour.
- Transaction boundaries and partial-failure behaviour.
- Disposable test databases and production-data protections.
- No hidden terminal-row edits or fabricated ready indexes.

Explain what runs database-independently and what requires PostgreSQL.

### C. Anchor-to-chunk resolution

Follow the accepted Prompt 108 rules:
- Relevance unit is a distinct authorized chunk ID.
- Resolve each gold passage to every eligible chunk containing its full required span.
- Missing or ambiguous mappings fail unless an explicit multi-chunk annotation resolves them.
- Deduplicate when multiple anchors map to one chunk.
- Pin the chunker version and verify the relevant chunk manifest.
- Account for repeated table headers as separate source spans.
- Respect snapshot-relative supersession and distinguish forbidden historical revisions from revisions valid in an older captured snapshot.
- Do not derive ground truth from whichever results retrieval happened to return.

Specify exact mapping inputs, outputs and failure cases.

### D. Retrieval evaluation and Recall

Use existing production retrieval seams, not a replacement ranking implementation.

For nonempty gold set G:
Recall@k = |set(top_k_chunk_ids) intersect G| / |G|

Required:
- k=5 and k=8.
- Per-question values and macro mean over nonempty gold sets.
- Empty gold yields N/A and is excluded from the macro mean, with excluded count reported.
- All-empty suites yield N/A, never 1.
- Duplicate retrieval IDs are contract errors.
- Fewer than k results are handled without changing the denominator.
- Report variants and profiles separately.
- Foreign or forbidden results fail isolation even when recall is high.
- Distinguish retrieval contract correctness from measured Recall.
- No fabricated minimum Recall threshold or semantic-quality claim for offline hashing.
- Clearly identify any proposed threshold requiring reviewer approval.

Cover deterministic examples including 2/3 recall, shared-chunk anchors, missing mappings, duplicated results, empty gold and all-empty suites.

### E. Scope boundaries

Keep M4e focused on corpus, mapping, retrieval contracts and Recall.

Defer:
- Model-generated report judgments and support precision.
- End-to-end injection resistance and output-canary behaviour.
- Live model/provider quality and cost evaluation.
- Review workflow, approval endpoints and snapshot persistence.
- Voyage adapter implementation.
- GUI or deployment additions.

Ground-truth fields needed later may be specified now without claiming their later metrics execute in M4e.

Do not change the accepted M4d trust model or ranking rules.

### F. Commands, outputs, tests and CI

Propose:
- Module placement consistent with current import boundaries.
- A minimal operator/test entry point, explaining whether an existing evaluation CLI should be extended or introduced.
- Output schema, deterministic ordering and reproducibility metadata.
- Safe diagnostics and exit codes.
- Database-independent tests and real PostgreSQL acceptance tests.
- Which checks should run in existing CI jobs and whether any workflow/wheel changes are needed.
- Packaging of corpus resources versus repository-only fixtures.
- An intended-file list for the later implementation.

No new dependency unless necessary. Identify any dependency proposal and its policy implications; do not install anything.

Do not broaden the container smoke by default. If an additional check is proposed, explain its value and scope for review.

### G. Decisions for review

- A clear recommendation.
- Alternatives and practical tradeoffs.
- Whether it changes an accepted decision or only fills in implementation detail.

Do not present recommendations as already approved.

## 3. Correction A: lifecycle phases and snapshot timing

The proposed per-document loop creates all revisions before the described initial capture. Rewrite it as explicit global phases:

1. Validate the entire corpus and ground truth before database writes.
2. Seed tenants and create or verify vendors.
3. Create and fully ingest/index revision 1 for every document.
4. Capture initial snapshots for each required tenant/vendor while those r1 revisions are genuinely active and ready.
5. Retain those trusted snapshot values in memory.
6. Apply later revisions in manifest order through real ingestion and indexing.
7. Capture final snapshots.
8. Evaluate both the retained initial snapshots and final snapshots after later revisions have activated.

Specify the exact responsibilities and outputs of loading versus evaluation orchestration. The implementation must not fabricate an initial snapshot after supersession.

Keep real production activation and indexing paths unchanged. No direct status edits, synthetic ready indexes or durable snapshot persistence are added.

Planned tests must prove:
- Initial capture occurs before any r2 activation.
- Final capture occurs after all intended replacements are ready.
- Initial-snapshot retrieval after replacement uses the old revision.
- Final retrieval uses the new revision and excludes the old one.

## 4. Correction B: repeat invocation and failure behaviour

The original repeat-run wording cannot require a superseded r1 to become active again.

Define separate contracts for:
- Fresh two-epoch evaluation.
- Idempotent loading or verification of an already loaded corpus.

Required rules:
- A repeat load accepts an already-settled historical revision in its correct superseded state.
- It verifies content, metadata, revision numbers, lifecycle states, manifests, ready indexes and canonical jobs.
- It creates no duplicate rows or jobs and does not reset terminal jobs.
- It does not reactivate old revisions.
- It does not claim to recapture the historical initial epoch.
- A fresh two-epoch run requires a fresh guarded disposable database, unless its original trusted initial snapshots are still explicitly available in memory.
- Define what a partially loaded or conflicting database causes the test-only orchestrator to do. Do not silently resume in a way that invents a missing epoch.

If the simplest contract is that fresh two-epoch evaluation refuses nonfresh state while a separate repeat-load verifier proves idempotency, specify that plainly.

For vendor reuse, account for the real create_vendor behaviour:
- create_vendor generates a UUID4.
- A duplicate slug raises DuplicateVendorSlugError after flush.
- A failed transaction must be rolled back before further queries.
Describe a valid tenant-scoped lookup/create/conflict strategy; do not imply that create_vendor itself returns an existing vendor.

Worker exit code is not job success. Read the actual expected job/revision/index outcome. Keep bounded claim counts and fixed failures explicit.

Add planned tests for superseded-r1 repeat loading, metadata conflict, partial-state refusal and no additional rows/jobs.

## 5. Correction C: complete reference and epoch schemas

Provide explicit TOML examples and exact fields for:

- Tenant-qualified anchor references, including foreign-tenant forbidden evidence.
- Vendor-qualified questions or unambiguous question ownership.
- Epoch applicability.
- Epoch-specific gold, forbidden evidence and authored labels where they differ.

Anchor IDs are currently unique only within a tenant, so bare IDs cannot identify another tenant's canaries safely. Choose one canonical qualified reference representation and validate every reference.

A common question definition may contain per-epoch cases, but make the format precise.

For example, retention labels and supporting claims must match the documents actually eligible in that epoch:
- Initial r1 evidence is not automatically the final r2 evidence.
- A later revision absent from an initial snapshot is forbidden for that snapshot.
- A superseded r1 may remain valid for a retained initial snapshot.

Clarify forbidden mapping:
- Resolve it against the relevant corpus revisions, including revisions outside the snapshot.
- Do not filter forbidden mappings down to the authorized snapshot, which would erase the traps.
- Keep gold eligibility checks separate.
- A future-revision forbidden reference can be resolved after the complete corpus has loaded, while the initial snapshot itself must have been captured earlier.

Validate acceptable and wrong claims' quotation references without treating their later support judgments as M4e execution.

Add planned tests for duplicate local anchor IDs across tenants, cross-tenant references, unknown references, contradictory gold/forbidden sets and epoch-specific labels.

## 6. Correction D: reproducibility and canonical report claims

Correct the determinism scope using the actual production identifiers:

- Vendor, document and revision IDs use UUID4.
- Chunk IDs are deterministic from tenant, revision, chunker version and ordinal, so they inherit fresh revision identities.
- Snapshot digests include captured_at.
- Ranking breaks ties by chunk UUID.

Therefore:
- Canonical serialization means identical validated report fields encode identically.
- Repeated evaluation with the same stored corpus, snapshot values, profile, queries and database behaviour can be deterministic.
- Fresh database loads need not produce identical IDs, manifests, snapshot digests, ranks or Recall values when UUID ties matter.
- Removing a top-level timestamp does not remove the timestamp already represented by snapshot.sha256.
- No cross-fresh-load byte or exact-metric equality is promised.

Do not change production UUID generation, capture time, tie-breaking or snapshot contracts to obtain stronger determinism.

Human-readable logical source references may accompany actual IDs for comparison, but do not claim that replacing IDs in a report makes tied rankings reproducible.

E7 remains report-only. A future proposed regression baseline must define the stable inputs and permitted variability; CI observation alone does not justify exact Recall pins across fresh random-ID corpora.

Add planned tests distinguishing:
- Canonical encoding of the same report value.
- Repeated retrieval from the same retained snapshots.
- Two independent fresh loads, with no false equality requirement.

## 7. Correction E: exact anchor/parts contract

Make the multi-chunk annotation implementable:

- Specify the exact type and fields of each part.
- Resolve each part within the already selected parent quote occurrence.
- Define occurrence disambiguation relative to that parent range.
- Require nonempty, ordered, nonoverlapping parts.
- Define permitted gaps using the production omission rules precisely.
- Reject annotations that silently discard substantive text.
- Each part must map to actual containing chunk body/header spans.
- Preserve all required containing chunks and deduplicate IDs.

The mapping output must represent provenance per mapping:
- An anchor can map through a body in one chunk and repeated headers in other chunks.
- A single anchor-level via flag cannot represent that.
- Specify entries containing chunk ID, relevant source span and body/header route, or an equivalent unambiguous structure.

Clarify the distinction between:
- Missing text.
- Ambiguous text occurrence.
- A source quote spanning a chunk boundary.
- An explicit valid multi-part annotation.
- A quote that would falsely concatenate a repeated header and non-adjacent body.

State any extra bounds for parts and mappings. Add planned tests covering each case.

## 8. Correction F: concrete encoding and schema contracts

Complete the proposed corpus/report contracts without implementing them:

- Exact required/optional fields and unknown-key rejection.
- Exact epoch field representation.
- Validated profile/configuration identity and report grouping.
- JSON representation of exact Recall fractions and N/A.
- Defined four-decimal display rounding, separate from exact arithmetic.
- What happens on contract/isolation failure: whether a fixed failure report is emitted, an error is raised, or both.
- Ordinary error privacy and process-control propagation, without exposing raw database exceptions.
- Input byte bounds before parsing or reading excessive corpus data.
- Path containment rules for manifest-referenced files, including traversal and symlink escape.

The corpus digest must use an unambiguous versioned encoding:
- Sorted normalized relative paths.
- Exact file bytes.
- Explicit framing, such as length-prefixing.
- Defined included/excluded file set and variant selection.
- No hash over unframed path-and-content concatenation.
- Do not hash the output report into its own corpus digest.

The pure retrieval modules parse bytes/validated values only. File-system handling stays in worker/tests and preserves existing import boundaries.

Any newly necessary design choice must be labelled as a recommendation awaiting review, rather than being silently treated as settled.

## 3. Make verify_loaded genuinely read-only

The current proposal calls seed_demo, create_upload and enqueue_index_revision, then promises no new rows or jobs.

That promise fails on missing or partial state:
- seed_demo can create missing records.
- create_upload can create a missing revision or enqueue work.
- enqueue_index_revision can create missing profile/index/job state.
- Comparing counts after those calls does not prevent committed changes.

Replace verify_loaded with a genuinely read-only verifier:
- No seed_demo.
- No create_upload or create_revision.
- No ensure_profile, create_index or enqueue calls.
- No worker.
- No new snapshot capture.
- No DML or repair.
- Read existing tenants/users, vendors, documents, revisions, profiles, chunk sets, indexes, embeddings and canonical jobs as needed.
- Verify exact expected metadata, content, revision numbers, lifecycle states, manifests, ready indexes and succeeded canonical jobs.
- Accept historical r1 as superseded where a later revision exists.
- Refuse missing, extra, unsettled, failed or conflicting corpus state with a fixed error.
- Define whether extra-state rejection is corpus-tenant-wide or limited to named corpus vendors, consistently with the freshness check.
- Use an explicitly read-only transaction with a consistent view for the verification. Ground the transaction handling in existing helpers rather than changing them.

Identify the required read statements and module placement. Evaluation-only SQL may live in the worker orchestrator if compatible with existing import boundaries; otherwise propose the narrowest necessary read seam and list its intended file explicitly. Do not implement it now.

Preserve production-seam idempotency coverage separately:
- After a complete fresh load, planned tests may call the existing upload and indexing seams on known complete records to demonstrate reuse and unchanged rows/jobs.
- Those tests are distinct from verify_loaded.
- Specify transaction handling and what is asserted.
- Do not use mutating probes to determine whether a partial database is complete.

Add planned tests:
- The verifier on a complete database performs no writes.
- Each relevant missing-state case refuses without changing database state.
- Metadata conflicts refuse without changes.
- Superseded-r1 verification succeeds.
- Production-seam reuse on a complete corpus creates no additional rows/jobs.
- No initial epoch is fabricated or recaptured.

Update N3 and all repeat-run descriptions consistently.

## 4. Restore complete quote and occurrence validation

The Prompt 141 rewrite removed the earlier quote-validation paragraph. Section C still refers to “anchor quote rules (A)”, but those rules no longer exist.

Define the exact rules in section A for both parent and part quotes:
- Exact string type.
- Nonempty and bounded code-point length.
- Strict UTF-8 encodability, with no NUL or unpaired surrogate.
- Exact source matching: no case folding, whitespace normalization or Unicode normalization.
- Explicit leading/trailing whitespace rules.
- Explicit multiline rules compatible with source-contiguous multi-part quotes and table spans.
- Optional occurrence is an exact positive integer, never bool, counted over non-overlapping matches.
- Missing occurrence for repeated matches and out-of-range occurrence have fixed outcomes.
- Parent occurrence is resolved in the revision text.
- Part occurrence is resolved only within the selected parent range.
- Unknown fields are rejected.

Keep the existing full-coverage, ordering, gap and provenance rules for parts.

Do not restore a restriction that makes the accepted cross-chunk annotation unusable. If multiline body quotes are permitted, state that explicitly and retain exact source offsets.

Add planned tests for empty quotes, invalid types, zero/negative/bool occurrences, invalid Unicode, bounds, multiline quotes and exact matching without normalization.

## 5. Define failure-report metrics precisely

The current proposal records contract and isolation failures in a complete report, but still requires ordinary Recall fields.

Specify:
- A question with any contract or isolation failure is invalid for Recall.
- Its recall_at_5 and recall_at_8 are null.
- This null is distinguishable from valid empty-gold N/A through an explicit question outcome/status or reason.
- Invalid questions are counted separately from excluded_empty_gold.
- Group output must clearly indicate failure.
- Do not present a failed group’s macro as an ordinary successful evaluation.

Recommended simple rule:
- If any question in a group has a contract or isolation failure, both group macro Recall fields are null.
- Retain explicit counts for total questions, valid nonempty-gold questions, valid empty-gold questions and invalid questions.
- require_passing fails the run regardless of other groups’ values.

Define reporting for malformed output:
- Duplicate IDs, bad ranks and out-of-snapshot results can be represented as failures without silently repairing or deduplicating the ranked output.
- If a returned chunk has no known logical source reference, its report entry can use an explicit null/unknown mapping rather than causing report construction to lose the original violation.
- Do not emit document/query text or arbitrary object representations.
- Only validated safe identifiers may appear in diagnostics.
- Operational retrieval/database failures may remain fixed EvaluationError with no complete report; distinguish these from inspectable contract/isolation violations.
- Define which report fields can be absent/null in a failure case, so the schema is implementable.

Add planned tests:
- Duplicate result IDs.
- A forbidden result.
- A foreign or unknown chunk.
- A snapshot/profile/configuration mismatch.
- Valid empty gold versus invalid-question null.
- Failed-group macro suppression.
- require_passing fails even when unaffected questions have perfect Recall.

Keep successful Recall arithmetic unchanged and report-only. No minimum threshold.

### Corpus and strict parsing

### Pure evaluation modules
Use the accepted evidenceguard_retrieval.evaluation placement for:

### Test-only worker orchestration
Implement:
- run_fresh_two_epoch
- verify_loaded
- evaluate

Preserve the accepted global lifecycle phases:
- Validate first.
- Refuse existing corpus state before writes.
- Seed and create vendors through production seams.
- Fully ingest/index all r1 revisions.
- Capture and retain genuine initial snapshots before later revisions exist.
- Apply later revisions through production ingestion/indexing.
- Capture final snapshots.
- Evaluate both retained epochs after replacement.

No direct status editing, fabricated ready indexes, terminal-job resets, durable snapshot storage or automatic recovery.

Read actual job/revision/index outcomes. Worker exit status alone is insufficient.

### Read-only verifier
- Use one consistent READ ONLY transaction through the existing unchanged helper.
- No seed/create/enqueue/worker/DML calls.
- Enumerate all corpus-tenant profiles and compare exactly with HASH_IDENTITY.
- Verify expected metadata, content, lifecycle states, manifests, indexes, counts and canonical jobs.
- Reject missing, partial, conflicting or extra state without changing rows.
- Never recreate initial snapshots.
- Keep production-seam reuse tests separate from verification.

### Reports and failures
- Successful Recall remains report-only with no threshold.
- Empty gold is valid N/A.
- Contract or isolation failure makes the question invalid, with null Recall.
- Invalid questions are separate from empty-gold exclusions.
- Any invalid question fails its group and suppresses both group macro values.
- require_passing fails regardless of perfect results elsewhere.
- Preserve observed ranked output; do not repair duplicates or discard forbidden results.
- Unknown logical references remain explicit nulls.
- Operational failures produce fixed errors rather than misleading reports.
- Preserve process-control exceptions and avoid retaining raw exception content.

### Determinism
Preserve production UUIDs, timestamps and tie-breaking.

Do not assert equality of IDs, digests, tied ranks or Recall across fresh databases. Canonical serialization applies to identical validated report values; repeated retrieval uses the same retained snapshots.

## 3. Finding A: complete validation before database writes

Current build_suite validates schemas and references but never locates or maps anchors. run_fresh_two_epoch then starts writing, while missing/ambiguous/unmappable anchors are discovered only during evaluate.

Implement one complete pure validation path before fresh-run database work:
- Locate every anchor against its selected variant's source text.
- Check occurrences, parts, ordering/gaps and chunk containment using the pinned production chunker.
- Validate every defined anchor, not just anchors used as gold.
- Reject missing, ambiguous, out-of-range and unmappable annotations before freshness queries, seed_demo, vendor creation or any other write.
- Validate both selected clean and injected content correctly.
- Keep later stored-manifest verification; offline validation does not replace it.

Keep module boundaries clean. Avoid a corpus/anchors circular import. A small pure orchestration helper in the appropriate evaluation module is allowed if necessary; record the placement.

Ensure run_fresh_two_epoch cannot bypass this complete validation merely because its caller supplied a Suite object. Do not rely only on a function name or a frozen outer dataclass.

Add regression tests:
- Nonexistent parent quote.
- Repeated quote without occurrence.
- Out-of-range occurrence.
- Invalid parts or a boundary-crossing quote without required parts.
- An invalid anchor used only as forbidden evidence.
- A valid committed corpus and both variants.
- Invalid suite rejected before any database/creation seam is called, using a factory double that records or refuses access.

Keep ground truth independent of retrieval output.

## 4. Finding B: return vendor identity only after successful transaction completion

Current ensure_vendor appends the new ID inside the transaction. If commit raises, the ordinary exception is swallowed and the nonempty list causes that ID to be returned.

Correct it:
- A created ID is returned only after the transaction context exits successfully.
- Commit/flush/setup/cleanup failure must not become successful creation.
- Ordinary failures produce a fresh fixed corpus_vendor_failed outside exception handlers, without original message, cause or context.
- DuplicateVendorSlugError still rolls back before lookup in a new transaction.
- Re-read and compare the concurrent vendor's name.
- Process-control exceptions must not be classified as a duplicate or ordinary success.

Add deterministic tests with transaction doubles:
- Successful create and commit.
- create_vendor failure.
- Commit failure after create_vendor returned an ID.
- Duplicate slug followed by matching re-read.
- Duplicate slug followed by mismatched or missing re-read.
- Private marker text absent from the normalized exception chain and formatted traceback.
- Process-control propagation.

Do not change the existing vendor store or transaction helper.

## 5. Finding C: preserve read failures through cleanup

The new evaluation read wrappers repeat the cleanup problem fixed in M4d:
a process-control exception from setup can be replaced by rollback/close failure, which _guard then converts to EvaluationError.

Correct all evaluation read paths:
- Freshness reads.
- Job/status reads.
- verify_loaded.
- Stored-span reads.
- Any other read_snapshot use introduced here.

Required behaviour:
- Preserve the original process-control exception object when ordinary cleanup failure replaces it.
- Preserve the first recorded semantic refusal if ordinary cleanup also fails.
- Normalize ordinary operational failures to fresh fixed errors outside handlers.
- If the body succeeded but cleanup failed, return no successful result.
- Do not inspect arbitrary exception chains to infer semantic failures.
- Do not log or retain raw SQL/backend exception text.
- Do not change document_views.read_snapshot or earlier M4d source.

Use a focused evaluation-owned boundary, taking account of the actual helper's setup and cleanup order. Reuse an appropriate existing public seam only if its contract fits; do not import private M4d machinery casually.

Add a deterministic fake-session matrix covering:
- KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.
- SET TRANSACTION, clock_timestamp and body.
- Ordinary rollback failure, close failure, both, and no cleanup failure.
- Process control raised by cleanup itself.
- Semantic refusal plus cleanup failure.
- Ordinary setup/body failures remaining private.
- Successful body plus cleanup failure returning no result.

Test actual evaluation entry points or their shared boundary, not only an unrelated helper.

## 6. Finding D: enforce aggregate bounds before payload reads

Current load_suite reads the files, then build_suite checks MAX_FILE_SET_BYTES. Thus an over-budget file set is read before rejection.

After reading the bounded manifest and deriving the file set:
- Validate paths and file metadata.
- Check per-file bounds and selected effective-set aggregate size before reading document/ground-truth payloads.
- Account explicitly for clean files additionally needed to validate injected replacements.
- Bound actual reads and recheck actual byte lengths and totals.
- Do not use an unrestricted read_bytes followed only by a length check where the read can exceed its budget.
- Preserve symlink, regular-file, containment and unexpected-file rejection.
- Keep the digest's accepted effective-file-set definition unchanged.

Add instrumented reader tests proving:
- An aggregate-over-budget set is rejected before content payload reads.
- Individual oversized files are rejected before reading.
- A file whose actual data exceeds its reported size remains bounded and fails.
- Normal clean/injected corpus loading still succeeds.

No need to claim protection against every concurrent filesystem attack. State the implemented bounds precisely.

## 3. Narrow correction

The production helper performs:

session.execute(select(func.clock_timestamp())).scalar_one()

_RecordingSession records exceptions from session methods, but not exceptions raised by methods of the returned result. Thus the pending outcome misses process control from scalar_one.

Extend the evaluation-owned boundary so:
- KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit from the setup clock result's scalar_one are recorded.
- The same exception object escapes even if ordinary rollback, close or both fail.
- No successful value is returned.
- Ordinary scalar_one failures remain fresh private corpus_read_failed errors.
- Existing semantic-refusal precedence remains intact.
- Body result-consumption failures remain covered by the body boundary.
- Existing successful SQLAlchemy result access and iteration continue working.

Use the smallest appropriate adaptation around the setup result/session proxy. Do not build a general SQLAlchemy abstraction or alter:
- document_views.read_snapshot;
- earlier M4d code;
- SQLAlchemy itself;
- the accepted transaction order.

Do not infer process-control or semantic outcomes by searching arbitrary exception chains.
